fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Into a Diet Quiz
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the quiz, the matching logic, and the table behind it from one prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Matching questions from one prompt

Describe the patterns you want to match, such as a planner or a grazer. Emergent drafts the questions, maps each option to a pattern, and rewords any of them by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
A result screen for every pattern

Each result gets a title and a short description that reads as a preference, not a verdict. Takers see their match, what it means, and what the next step with you is.
fields.feature_3:
Email capture before the result

Ask for an email on the last screen and the app holds the result until it is entered. Every address lands beside that taker's answers, ready for your follow-up list.
fields.feature_4:
Every answer in a database you own

Each finished quiz is a row: the answers, the matched pattern, the email, and a timestamp. Filter the rows by pattern before a launch, or export them whenever you need to.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen on a phone

Takers answer one question at a time with a progress bar, which keeps a 10-question quiz under 3 minutes on a phone. Emergent puts no cap on how many people respond.
fields.feature_6:
Code and a domain that stay yours

The quiz runs on your own domain, which Emergent includes and bills in credits. Paid plans export the full code to your GitHub repository, and the next campaign starts from it.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Put a Diet Quiz to Work
fields.tab_content_1:
64 matched The Planner in March

Larkglen Nutrition matches every quiz taker to an eating pattern. In March, 212 people finished the quiz: 64 matched The Planner, 58 The Grazer, 49 The Winger, and 41 The Social. Each Planner match got an invite to the structured coaching track, and every answer sits in the studio's own database.
fields.tab_content_2:
448 takers typed an email to see a result

Rowanmere Kitchen sells weekly meal boxes and runs a box finder quiz on its site. The last screen asks for an email, and the result stays locked until an address goes in. 1,180 people finished the quiz and 448 left an address, each one saved beside the box they matched.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every score under 6 ends in a call

Granite Row Fitness gives every new member a short habit quiz at signup, and the app turns the answers into a habit score. A score under 6 books a trainer call, with the member's answers on the trainer's screen before it starts. Of the 31 who joined in April, 9 scored under 6.
fields.tab_content_4:
1,468 readers finished it on their phones

The Weekly Table sends a scored quiz to its readers with the Friday issue, 7 questions and a result band at the end. Last Friday, 2,406 readers opened it and 1,468 finished on their phones. The editor watches finishes land on a live dashboard.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Diet Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a diet quiz that matches takers to an eating pattern, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the job the quiz does
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write the results before the questions
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Draft questions that split the patterns
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what a finished quiz earns you before you write anything: coaching leads, box matches, or intake scores. One quiz does one job well. Put that job in your prompt, and Emergent builds the questions, the results, and the table around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A matching quiz maps every option to a result, which suits eating patterns and product picks. A scored quiz counts points and fits habit checks with bands at the end. Name the type in the prompt before any questions exist.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Draft each result as a short preference, such as a planner who shops once and cooks from a list. When the results are clear, every question has a target, and takers get a result that reads like them rather than a grade.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask about behavior, not goals: who cooks, when, and what a usual week holds. A good question sends different takers to different options. If every taker picks the same answer, the question splits nothing, so cut it or sharpen the options.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Gate the result with an email
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add an email field on the last screen and say what the address gets: the result plus one follow-up, nothing more. The app keeps the result behind that field and writes each address into the same row as its answers.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it with 5 people before launch
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the draft to 5 people who match your audience and watch where they stall. A question read two ways, an option nobody picks, a result that feels wrong: each shows up in minutes. Fix the wording by prompt and send it again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Watch the results table and prune
fields.howto_step_7_des: Check the table after the first 100 takers. A pattern almost nobody matches needs sharper questions, or should fold into a neighbor. Retire options that never get picked, and keep the quiz short enough to finish in one sitting.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a diet quiz for my nutrition coaching studio that matches every taker to 1 of 4 eating patterns.

faq_plan.a: A diet quiz is a short set of questions about how someone eats, turned into a result: an eating pattern, a habit score, or a product match. Coaches, meal brands, and gyms use one to match people to a program, a box, or a follow-up, and publishers run them to keep readers engaged.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a diet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe the quiz in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the patterns or score bands you want, the tone of the questions, and where answers should land. Emergent builds it from that prompt, and another prompt rewords a question or adds a pattern.

faq_plan.q: What diet is best for me free quiz?
faq_plan.ref: What diet is best for me free quiz?

prov.original: What diet is best for me free quiz?

faq_plan.a: Try the quiz on this page: 8 questions that match you to 1 of 4 eating patterns, with no signup. A quiz cannot tell you what to eat; it shows the pattern your answers lean toward. To publish a free diet quiz of your own, Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What diet quiz questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Write questions a taker can answer without thinking hard: a normal weeknight, a grocery run, eating out. Each question should separate at least two patterns, and every option should map to one result. A love language quiz runs on the same matching mechanics; only the subject changes.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a diet quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it between 6 and 10. Fewer than 6 gives the match little to work with; more than 10 asks a lot of someone on a phone. The quiz on this page runs 8 questions. If a question never changes anyone's result, it is padding: cut it.

faq_plan.q: How does a diet quiz match someone to an eating pattern?
faq_plan.a: Every option quietly points at one pattern. When someone finishes, the app counts the points per pattern and shows the one with the most; a tie goes to the result listed first. That is why options matter more than questions: each one is a small vote.

faq_plan.q: How do I get leads from a diet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Hold each result behind an email field, then send one follow-up tied to the pattern that taker matched. A quiz funnel takes it further: the result screen routes every pattern to its own offer. Emergent puts no response caps on a quiz, however big the traffic gets.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a nutritionist to make a diet quiz?
faq_plan.a: No, as long as the quiz recommends rather than prescribes. Keep results as preferences, such as a pattern your answers lean toward, and keep medical claims out of the copy. If the quiz feeds a coaching or nutrition business, have the practitioner review the results text before launch.

faq_plan.q: What should the result screen of a diet quiz say?
faq_plan.a: Three things: the name of the match, two or three sentences describing it in the taker's own terms, and one next step. Write it so a taker would happily screenshot it, and skip scores unless the quiz promised one. On Emergent, the result screen changes with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Where should a diet quiz live on my site?
faq_plan.a: Give the quiz its own page and link it from the places your audience already reads: recipe posts, the newsletter, and the signup flow. Keep the pattern names visible above the start button, since they are the hook. The same placement thinking applies to a spirit animal quiz or any other matching format.
